facts.text: Studies found 100 m of mangroves cut wave height by 13% to 66%, mostly for waves under 70 cm.

citation.title: Reduction of Wind and Swell Waves by Mangroves
citation.authors: McIvor, A.L., Möller, I., Spencer, T. and Spalding, M.
citation.publisher: The Nature Conservancy and Wetlands International (Natural Coastal Protection Series, Report 1)
citation.note: The report states that wave height can be reduced by between 13 and 66% over 100 m of mangroves, and that the research so far has focused on small waves (wave height < 70 cm).

facts.text: Research in England and Wales found sand dunes can be an important natural barrier against coastal flooding.

citation.title: Sand Dune Processes and Management for Flood and Coastal Defence: Summary (FD1302)
citation.authors: Pye, K., Saye, S. and Blott, S.
citation.publisher: Defra / Environment Agency Flood and Coastal Erosion Risk Management R&D Programme
citation.note: The summary says sand dune systems can provide an important natural coastal flood defence, whose importance lies in their function as barriers to coastal flooding, and discusses managing them as dynamic natural defences. The research is about dunes in England and Wales.

facts.text: Khazans are Goa's coastal wetlands, reclaimed from marsh. Bunds keep out the tide, and farmers and fishers share the land.

citation.title: The Khazans of Goa: A Socio-Cultural Perspective
citation.note: Describes khazans as a traditional agro-aqua integrated system practised by local communities for equitable sharing of resources between farmers and fishers, on land reclaimed from marshes, with bunds preventing the ingress of tidal waters and a sluice gate regulating the flow of water.

facts.text: The mangroves on a khazan's outer bund work as wave breakers against the tide.

citation.title: The Khazans of Goa: A Socio-Cultural Perspective
citation.note: States that the outer embankment comprises mangroves that act as wave breakers against tidal action.

facts.text: When a khazan bund breaks, mangroves grow back over the old fields.

citation.title: Mangroves and Khazan agriculture: Sustaining Goa's promise for fish, curry and rice
citation.note: Published 24 July 2020. Shows mangroves reclaiming khazan lands because of breaching bunds. A blog article, so the game shows this as reported by the author.

facts.text: A khazan holds floodwater, so nearby homes stay drier.
Mangroves take a few years to reach full strength, so plant them early.
Pandanus softens a surge a little, on sand where mangroves can't grow.
A dune that takes a beating isn't destroyed: it weakens for that storm and is still there for the next.
A seawall stops most of a surge while it holds, and it's strong from the day it's built.
A seawall pushed past its limit fails all at once, and the surge goes on past it.
A seawall lowers biodiversity: nothing in the game lives on it.
A breakwater sits out at sea and takes the force out of a cyclone's waves before they reach the beach.
A small dam holds the river back until a flood is too big, then fails all at once.
A small dam earns Coin and protects against floods, but it lowers biodiversity.
A resort earns Coin every season, but it lowers biodiversity and the city's resilience.
A resort defends nothing: a storm that reaches it does damage.
Sand mining earns more Coin than anything else, and it weakens the city against floods.
Sand mining lowers biodiversity more than any other build.
The Yacht does nothing for your defences or your resilience. It's there to be seen.
The Yacht is the most expensive thing you can build.
A mangrove forest is a coastal nursery for young fish, crabs and prawns.
Mangroves lock away carbon faster than almost any rainforest.

Sea turtles and shorebirds nest in the sand a healthy dune protects.
Barnacles, oysters and coral settle on a breakwater over time.
Mangroves and wetlands on Goa's coast have been cleared for waterfront rooms.
Sand taken from a riverbed is natural flood buffer lost.
Strip enough sand from a river and the sea creeps further upstream.
An anchor can flatten the seagrass beneath it.
